extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and researchers in media studies, digital culture, and humor/meme studies
extracted.subtask_description: Frameworks, empirical criteria, and methodological guidelines for analyzing, classifying, and assessing internet memes and memetic videos (e.g., selection criteria for spread, multimodal analytic dimensions, and diffusion measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic unit characteristics (content, form, stance, memetic landscape)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes conceived as digital units with shared characteristics: content, form, stance, and memetic landscape (Nissenbaum & Shifman referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a meme along these four dimensions: what the content communicates, the formal/visual/textual packaging, the attitude or stance it adopts toward its referent, and the broader memetic landscape (how it fits among related memes and topical trajectories). Use these axes to compare derivatives and locate a meme within participatory culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative/remixability as a defining property
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet artifacts that generate derivatives using imitation and remixing (Dynel & Messerli, 2020); represent participatory digital culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether and how readily a meme invites imitation, remix, or derivative works (templates, editable assets, modularity). High derivative potential indicates participatory affordances and likelihood of circulation and mutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic video attributes (Shifman): six common features
rubrics_metrics.description: Six common features of memetic videos: focus on ordinary people; flawed masculinity; humor; simplicity; repetitiveness; and whimsical content (Limor Shifman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist to profile memetic videos. Shifman notes each attribute marks the video as incomplete or flawed, thereby invoking further creative dialogue—so presence of several features suggests higher propensity for user-driven derivatives and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for meme spread (Heylighen, operationalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criteria hypothesized to predict meme survival/spread: utility, novelty, simplicity, coherence, authority, and proselytism (Heylighen, 1997; operationalization paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score memes on each criterion and test correlation with observed prevalence. Operationalization methods recommended include chain-transmission experiments (e.g., 'Chinese whispers'), computational simulations of social/cognitive processes, and correlational analyses between criterion scores and web frequency/visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical framework for political satire / imagefare
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework combining: goal with target, frame of reference with focus, and means with presentation (used to analyze political satire and imagefare in conflict contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing political memes, pair each rhetorical/strategic dimension: identify the meme's goal and its intended target; determine its frame of reference and what aspect it focuses on; and examine its means (tools, modalities) together with presentation style. Employ multimodal discourse analysis to inspect these linked pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Folkloric characteristics of memes
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes as modern folklore exhibiting attributes such as anonymity of authorship, rapid variation, and communal participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat memes as folkloric artifacts—document authorship anonymity, track mutational patterns, and consider community participation dynamics when evaluating cultural role, authenticity, and transmission pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal critical discourse analysis rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of socio-semiotic and critical discourse approaches (e.g., Theo van Leeuwen; Norman Fairclough) to examine linguistic and non-linguistic resources used to create meaning and impact in memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze both visual and verbal semiotic resources, their interaction, and how they construct persuasive/ideological effects. Code modalities (image, text, layout, color, intertextual references), and interpret how multimodal choices produce framing, solidarity-building, or other discursive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognisability, circulation potential, and platform visibility logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes materialise convergence by borrowing editorial/campaign frames and reworking them through meme grammars optimised for recognisability and circulation; they blur amateur/professional boundaries and are shaped by platform visibility logics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a meme's recognisability (how easily users identify and reuse it), circulation affordances (format, size, shareability), and how platform algorithms or norms might amplify or constrain it. Consider remix aesthetics, curation practices, and the attention/hope labour economy in assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web memetics diffusion methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for assessing meme diffusion: identify different versions, trace online evolution, and measure web presence and translations using extensive web searches combined with quantitative and qualitative analyses (Shifman & Thelwall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect corpora of meme instances, document variants and local adaptations, quantify frequency across platforms/languages, and qualitatively interpret mutation patterns. Use this method to evaluate global diffusion, translation effects, and persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memes as tactical social action / political efficacy criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes can function as 'tactics' for subaltern actors to challenge dominant power structures—allowing mobilization, persuasion, solidarity-building, or polarization depending on design and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess memes for tactical features: ability to mobilize action (calls to act, awareness-raising), persuasive framing, resonance with group identity, and potential for coalition-building or polarization. Examine contextual constraints (platform norms, repression) that affect whether meme 'wins' can be retained or translated into offline outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness measures for humor-based mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical consideration that humor type (e.g., feminist vs neutral memes), audience identity (e.g., feminist identity), and aversiveness moderate the effect of memes on collective-action proclivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In studies of mobilization, include moderator measurements (audience identity strength, perceived aversiveness) when testing whether humorous memes increase intentions to participate. Use experimental and survey methods to detect interaction effects.
